paragraphs: Friend, here's what this whole passage is about. Two kinds of wisdom are on the table, and you can tell them apart by what they grow. One is jealous and selfish, and James says where it lives, there will be "disorder and every evil practice" (James 3:16). The other is from above, "first of all pure, then peace-loving, gentle, accommodating, full of mercy and good fruit, impartial, and sincere" (James 3:17). So being wise isn't about being the smartest person in the room, it's about what your life is growing.

Now watch where James says the fights come from. He doesn't blame the neighbor, the boss, or the guy who took the last parking spot. He points to "the passions at war within you" (James 4:1). I know, I know, that stings a little, and I think it stings me too. But here's the good news, baker: when the trouble is inside, God can reach it. He says, "God opposes the proud, but gives grace to the humble" (James 4:6), and He "gives us more grace" (James 4:6).

So what do we do with that? James gives it straight: "Submit yourselves, then, to God. Resist the devil, and he will flee from you. Draw near to God, and He will draw near to you" (James 4:7-8). Then he says "Humble yourselves before the Lord, and He will exalt you" (James 4:10). That includes putting down the gavel on the people around you, because there is "only one Lawgiver and Judge" (James 4:12). Stay low, stay close to God, and let Him do the lifting. That's a recipe worth baking every single day.
